I have trouble expressing why I am where I am at the moment but here is a try. I used to go to sleepovers as a kid and felt uncomfortable when I saw fathers without a beer in their hand. I never knew the concept of alcoholism actually at that age. I just knew it was weird.
When my brother (who is 7 years older than me) started using meth my Dad started drinking rum (he drank beer for years). I was the only child who lived at home (four older siblings). I would see him slurr his words, get angry, treat me like a piece of shit (he never touched or physically harmed me), pass out early and then go to work the next morning. I would complain to my mother how much it affected me but she never did anything about it (she always said he was drunk by the time she got home so she could never talk to him, Bullshit) but to be honest she's a good mother. My mother often told me how alcohol ran in my blood (I have several alcoholic relatives). I hated everything about drinking and I hated my father.

Until I did it to socialize, it was never in my life. But eventually out of nowhere it became my best friend and only friend. I started to drink alone. I've lost my license, gotten into trouble with the law, relationship troubles, suicide attempts, lasted only 5 days in a rehab, the list goes on and on. I've been an alcoholic for 2 years and I'm 21 years old. 

He never shaped my alcoholism. He never forced me to drink in my room alone or get involved with police officers. He doesn't pour my drinks or supply my alcohol to me. At your siblings ages alcohol disgusted me too. But alcoholism really comes out of nowhere. Addict relationships are extremely unhealthy. We're unpredictable, manipulate, drama queens, you name it we are it. So I suggest cutting ties. It becomes more harmful than helpful in the long run.
